\begin{theorem}[Schwartz–Zippel bound]
\lean{Randomized.schwartz_zippel}
\proofsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p017-b001,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p017-b002
}
\label{Randomized.schwartz_zippel}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $m,d\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $p\in\mathbb{Z}[X_1,\ldots,X_m]$ be a nonzero polynomial
of total degree at most $d$. For any finite nonempty set $S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$, the
fraction of tuples in $S^m$ at which $p$ is nonzero is at least $1-d/|S|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial zero count over a finite set]
\lean{Randomized.two_mul_card_eval_eq_zero_le}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p017-b001,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p017-b002
}
\label{Randomized.two_mul_card_eval_eq_zero_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $R$ be a commutative integral domain, let $m$ be a natural number, and let $p$ be a
nonzero polynomial in $m$ variables over $R$. For a finite nonempty set $S\subseteq R$
with $2\deg(p)\le |S|$, at most half of the functions $f:\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\to S$ satisfy
$p(f)=0$; equivalently, twice the number of such functions is at most $|S|^m$.
\end{theorem}
